output.notes: Described the all-shared, E=128 ALBERT. The headline model is ALBERT-xxlarge (12 layers, H=4096, 64 heads), trained with MLM+SOP and no dropout. primary_config is base because it is the smallest configuration reported. block_ops use base sizes. Heads come from the table that lists Heads; they are consistent with the H/64 rule. d_ff is computed from the stated 4H rule. head_dim 64 is implied by heads = H/64. The paper only says ALBERT is 'similar to BERT', which is not an explicit inheritance, so I did not inherit anything. Left not_stated: norm type and placement, positional embeddings, biases, GELU approximation, embedding tying, segment embeddings and head structure. No norm ops appear in block_ops because the paper never describes them. Parameter counts differ slightly between the two tables (59M/60M; 233M/235M). The ensembles also use 24-layer xxlarge.
